name: Community Animals Partners and Welfare Advocates (CAPWA UP)
description: CAPWA UP is a recognized student organization at UP Diliman that looks after the campus's community dogs and cats, known locally as 'iskats'. It runs regular feeding programs, donation drives and awareness activities, and pushes for the adoption of abandoned campus animals. Volunteer openings are announced on the group's Facebook page.
volunteer_activities: feeding programs for campus dogs and cats
coordinating adoption of abandoned campus animals
how_to_join: Follow the CAPWA UP Facebook page and respond to its posts calling for volunteers for feeding programs, donation drives and other campus activities.

name: Coron Animal Savers
description: Coron Animal Savers is a volunteer-run rescue and shelter for stray and abandoned dogs and cats in Coron, Palawan, caring for more than 100 animals. Its work combines shelter care, street feeding missions and community education, and it reports over 400 sterilizations and vaccinations carried out so far. The group is supported by local dive shops, resorts and tour operators.
volunteer_activities: shelter care: bathing, nail trimming and grooming
street feeding routes in the evening
photography and social media content for adoptable animals
how_to_join: Organise volunteering through the site's volunteer page or by messaging Coron Animal Savers on Facebook or Instagram, where they post openings and roles.

name: DLSU PUSA (Professors for the Upliftment of Society's Animals)
description: DLSU PUSA brings together students, faculty, staff and alumni who care for the stray cats of De La Salle University's Manila campus. Members feed the cats, coordinate neutering and veterinary treatment, and work on rehoming, alongside awareness activities on campus. The group has been active since 2015 and recruits volunteers from the university community.
how_to_join: Join the DLSU PUSA Facebook group and watch for calls to feed, transport or foster campus cats; the group is oriented toward the DLSU community.

name: Furvent Animal Rescue and Advocacy
description: Furvent is a Baguio-based registered nonprofit, founded in 2020, that rescues, rehabilitates and rehomes dogs and cats and runs what local fundraising pages describe as the city's only active shelter. Volunteers help with kennel care, cleaning, giving medicines and hands-on time with the rescues. The group also works with city authorities on animal rescue operations, including after the August 2026 Baguio landslide.
volunteer_activities: administering medications and monitoring sick rescues
how_to_join: Message Furvent Animal Rescue and Advocacy through its Facebook page to ask about shelter volunteering or to join upcoming donation and feeding drives.

name: IVHQ — Animal Care in Palawan
description: A volunteer-abroad program run by International Volunteer HQ that places international volunteers in a local animal shelter in Palawan, caring for rescued dogs and cats. IVHQ's Philippines programs run year-round out of Palawan, with other projects in teaching, healthcare and environmental conservation. The program fee covers accommodation, meals and local project placement.
volunteer_activities: promoting responsible pet ownership in the community
how_to_join: Apply online through IVHQ, pay the registration fee to secure your place, then pick a start date — programs begin every Monday.
requirements: Volunteers must be aged 17 or older (families accepted), commit to 3–5 hours a day for 1 to 24 weeks, and pay program fees starting from USD 390 per week.

name: Pawssion Project Foundation
description: Pawssion Project runs a shelter in Tungkong Mangga, San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan (and a second one in Bacolod) for rescued dogs and cats, having taken in thousands of animals since 2018. Time spent with the rescues is treated as part of their rehabilitation, so volunteers mainly focus on enrichment and routine care. Walk-in volunteers are accepted during published shelter hours.
volunteer_activities: CSR, school and group volunteering events
how_to_join: Book a Bulacan shelter visit through the Jotform link on their volunteer page, then drop by Tuesday to Sunday, 10 AM to 5 PM.
requirements: Visits must be booked in advance; anyone bringing their own pets must show proof that vaccinations are up to date, and volunteers are asked to check with caretakers before interacting with a rescue.

name: Wildlife In Need Foundation (WIN)
description: WIN is a US-founded nonprofit registered in the Philippines with its headquarters in Subic Bay, Zambales, where it runs a wildlife rescue center and an animal care clinic. It takes in and rehabilitates confiscated and injured wildlife — including macaques, giant fruit bats, reptiles, sea turtles and marine mammals — while also caring for horses and companion animals. The group explicitly welcomes international volunteers and interns.
volunteer_activities: preparing food, cleaning cages and enrichment for rescue animals
joining rescue teams for sick or injured wildlife, turtles and marine mammals
assisting horse care at El Kabayo Stables
how_to_join: Contact WIN through the volunteer and intern page on their site to ask about current placements at the Subic Bay rescue center and education programs.
requirements: Volunteers must be willing to live and work at the center; veterinary internships require completion of at least the second year of veterinary study, and other internships are screened on criteria for the field of interest.

name: Bantay Pawikan, Inc. — Pawikan Conservation Center
description: Bantay Pawikan runs the Pawikan Conservation Center in Nagbalayong, Morong, a community-based hatchery and sanctuary that protects nesting sea turtles on Bataan's west coast. Its volunteers — many of them former egg collectors — patrol the beaches, transfer clutches to the hatchery and release hatchlings, and the center also hosts visitors and the annual Pawikan Festival.
volunteer_activities: night beach patrols for nesting turtles
how_to_join: Sign up through the volunteer form linked from the Pawikan Conservation Center Facebook page (slots are limited and must be reserved) or visit the center in Morong to help with hatchery work and releases.
requirements: Volunteer slots are limited and advance registration is required; specific conditions are announced per placement.

name: LAMAVE (Large Marine Vertebrates Research Institute Philippines)
description: LAMAVE is a Filipino marine conservation and research nonprofit based in Puerto Princesa, Palawan that studies whale sharks, sea turtles, sharks and rays across the archipelago. Volunteers join field teams for turtle nesting beach patrols, photo-identification surveys and shark catch monitoring, and are trained in the group's research methods. Placements run for weeks to months so volunteers contribute usable data to conservation work.
volunteer_activities: whale shark photo-identification and survey work
shark catch monitoring with local fishers
how_to_join: Submit the volunteer application form on the LAMAVE site for a specific project and placement date, then commit to the full minimum placement period on site.
requirements: At least 21 years old, a minimum one-month commitment (longer for some projects), a donation contribution that supports the project, and your own medical insurance and travel to the site; scuba-based projects require diving insurance.

name: Philippine Animal Rescue Team (PART)
description: PART runs a no-kill sanctuary in Santa Elena, Camarines Norte that is home to rescued dogs and cats as well as farm animals, including goats. It also runs a stray feeding program, provides vaccinations and spay/neuter care, and sends teams to disasters such as the Taal volcano eruption. Volunteers are recruited through its website and social media pages.
volunteer_activities: assisting rescue and disaster response missions
how_to_join: Send a message through the volunteer page on phanimalrescueteam.info or contact the team on Facebook to arrange a visit or join feeding and rescue activities.

name: Dogs Mountain
description: Dogs Mountain runs a dog sanctuary in Naguilian, La Union and organizes international volunteer placements built around free rabies vaccination campaigns. Volunteers spend two-week sessions setting up vaccination clinics, doing door-to-door work in nearby communities and running rabies education, alongside daily sanctuary care. Vets, veterinary nurses, students and non-veterinary volunteers can all apply.
volunteer_activities: mass rabies vaccination drives and mobile clinics
community education on rabies and responsible pet ownership
logistics, animal handling and data entry for non-vet volunteers
how_to_join: Apply through the volunteer form on dogsmountain.org, choose one of the published two-week session dates, and secure your place with the required deposit before paying the program fee.
requirements: Ages 18–55; proof of rabies vaccination within the past two years (or a titre within three months), current tetanus vaccination, and comprehensive travel insurance; licensed vets and nurses must supply copies of their licences, and a paid program fee applies.

name: Animal Kingdom Foundation (AKF)
description: AKF runs a large rescue and rehabilitation center in Capas, Tarlac that takes in abused and neglected animals, including dogs saved from the dog-meat trade. Its programs include rescue and rehoming, a low-cost clinic, and campaigns against the dog-meat trade and for cage-free keeping. The group regularly invites volunteers and 'voluntourists' to work at the center.
volunteer_activities: voluntourism stays at the rescue center
how_to_join: Fill out the AKF Volunteers Recruitment Form linked from the contact page or message the page so the team can assign you to a volunteer group; orientation schedules are announced on their Facebook page.
requirements: No specific requirements are stated — applicants simply complete the volunteer recruitment form, and their orientation posts say no experience is needed.

name: Biyaya Animal Care / Biyaya Animal Sanctuary
description: Biyaya operates a sanctuary in Alfonso, Cavite for rescued animals together with clinics and a dedicated spay/neuter facility in Metro Manila. The organization runs several volunteer tracks, including shelter volunteering, adoption drives and 'Biyayanihan' kapon outreach missions that need both veterinary and non-veterinary helpers. It says the sanctuary cares for more than 1,500 rescued animals.
volunteer_activities: sanctuary volunteering at the Alfonso shelter
Sanctuary in the City adoption drives
Biyayanihan kapon (spay/neuter) outreach as a vet or non-vet
how_to_join: Use the 'Biyaya Volunteer Sign Up' form on biyaya.ph, pick a role (sanctuary, adoption drive, or kapon outreach), and wait for orientation and shelter-day announcements.
requirements: No specific requirements are listed on the site; kapon outreach has separate sign-up options for veterinary and non-veterinary volunteers.

name: CARA Welfare Philippines
description: CARA is a volunteer-driven, donation-funded group that works with stray cats and dogs across Metro Manila instead of running a traditional shelter. It maintains a cat facility in Mandaluyong and a dog facility in Novaliches, Quezon City, alongside adoption, foster and catch-neuter-vaccinate-return (CNVR) programs. Volunteers also help with school talks, community coordination and content creation.
volunteer_activities: adoption and fostering support (application review, home visits, turnover)
how_to_join: Email admin@caraphil.org with 'Media Team Volunteer' in the subject line to be considered now, or message the CARA page to be queued for the next orientation once general sign-ups reopen.
requirements: 18 years or older, a commitment of 20 hours of volunteer work per quarter, and full support of CARA's philosophy and policies; general volunteer sign-ups are currently on hold while they review Content & Media Team applicants.

name: Philippine Animal Welfare Society (PAWS)
description: PAWS is one of the country's oldest animal welfare NGOs and runs the PAWS Animal Rehabilitation Center in Loyola Heights, a shelter funded entirely by donations. Volunteers do day-to-day animal care such as walking, bathing and kennel cleaning, and also help with humane education, adoption counseling, fundraising events and disaster-relief rescues. The group additionally operates a low-cost spay/neuter (kapon) program and outreach drives.
volunteer_activities: direct animal care (dog walking, bathing, grooming, feeding, cage cleaning)
shelter feeding and cleaning group programs
how_to_join: Submit the volunteer application form on the PAWS website and attend a scheduled volunteer orientation — the next one listed is 10 October 2026 — then choose a volunteer team.
requirements: Attend orientation and pay a P1,000 deposit (refunded after six consecutive months of at least 8 volunteer hours per month); pre-exposure rabies shots are required for direct animal care, and minors must attend with a parent or guardian.

name: Happy Animals Club
description: A Cebu-based no-kill shelter that began in 2014 when its then nine-year-old founder started feeding street dogs and the story went viral. It has rescued, rehabilitated and rehomed hundreds of dogs and cats and has organised large spay-and-neuter events with partner veterinary groups.
how_to_join: Reach the shelter through the contact form on their website or message their Facebook page to ask about current ways to help, since volunteer needs are announced on their social accounts.

name: Lyn's Animal Rescue
description: A small, home-run non-profit rescue on Siquijor Island founded by Lyn, who has been rescuing animals since she was 13. Its site lists dozens of dogs and cats in its care, all fed, sheltered and given medical support every day.
how_to_join: Contact them by WhatsApp on 0966 234 6043, through their Facebook page or Instagram, and let them know your availability and how you would like to help.
requirements: They ask only that volunteers be kind, reliable and willing to help.

name: Mayari Animal Rescue Organization (MARO)
description: One of the larger volunteer-run shelters in Cebu, with facilities in Guadalupe, Cebu City, working mainly with sick, malnourished and pound-scheduled street dogs and cats. All its adopted animals are vaccinated against rabies and spayed or neutered before rehoming.
how_to_join: Contact the shelter by email at mayarirescue@yahoo.com or through their Facebook page to arrange a visit; they regularly put out calls for dog walkers and shelter volunteers.

name: Moalboal Animal Welfare Organization
description: The animal welfare group recognised by the Municipal Government of Moalboal as a partner in responsible tourism and animal care. Its sanctuary volunteering — feeding, walking and bonding with rescued cats and dogs — has become the second most-searched activity for visitors to the town on TripAdvisor.
volunteer_activities: walking and bonding with shelter animals
general volunteer tasks at the sanctuary
how_to_join: Visitors coordinate their preferred schedule through the group's Instagram account @moalboalshelteroutpost or by calling 0915 0437628, according to the municipal government's announcement.

name: Ormoc Strays Oasis
description: A SEC-registered non-profit rescue and rehabilitation group in Ormoc City, Leyte, grown out of a small crew of volunteers feeding street animals. It rescues, vets, adopts out and rehomes dogs and cats while pushing responsible pet ownership, vaccination and spaying or neutering.
volunteer_activities: feeding, cleaning and caring for rescues
how_to_join: Fill out the volunteer sign-up form on their website and tell them how you would like to help; the team then contacts you to guide you through the next steps and schedule an orientation.
requirements: Open to individuals, students and groups; volunteers become part of an LGU-recognised volunteer network that provides training and certificates.

name: Pawssion Project Foundation — Bacolod Shelter
description: A non-profit rescue founded in 2018 whose first shelter was opened in Bacolod, now running a permanent sanctuary at Hacienda Feliza in Barangay Granada alongside its Bulacan shelter. It rescues, rehabilitates, spays/neuters and rehomes dogs and cats, reporting more than 3,000 animals rescued to date.
how_to_join: Walk-in volunteers are welcomed at the Bacolod shelter Tuesday to Sunday, 10AM to 5PM, but you should book an appointment through the shelter visit form on their website so the team expects you.
requirements: No formal requirements are stated for walk-in volunteers; if you bring your own pets you must show proof that their vaccinations are up to date.

name: Team Rescue Iloilo
description: An Iloilo City rescue group based in Ledesco Village, La Paz that says it has saved more than 300 dogs and cats and provides life-saving medical care and rehabilitation for its rescues. It repeatedly puts out open calls for volunteers and also helps coordinate spaying for rescued animals.
how_to_join: Watch for their volunteer calls on their Facebook page and message the page, or use the number they publish (0966-485-1773), to ask how you can help.

name: Philippine Tarsier Foundation, Inc.
description: A non-stock, non-profit founded in 1996 that implements the Philippine Tarsier Conservation Program with DENR and Department of Tourism backing, and runs the Tarsier Sanctuary in Corella. It combines habitat protection, research, community work and eco-tourism, and has a long history of hosting volunteers who stay on site.
how_to_join: Contact the Foundation directly through its Facebook page (the site's official contact link is Messenger to fb.com/tarsierfoundation) to ask about current volunteer slots, since volunteers are hosted on site.

name: Balyena at Lumba sa Pilipinas (Balyena.org)
description: A non-profit society established in 2013 that researches whales and dolphins around the Philippine archipelago and trains coastal communities in marine mammal stranding response. Members of the public can join its research and outreach work or act as eyes on the water by reporting sightings and strandings.
volunteer_activities: volunteering on research and outreach programs
reporting and assisting with marine mammal strandings
how_to_join: Use the 'Be A Volunteer' page on their site to get involved, and apply through their research expedition form when a trip is announced; sighting and stranding reports can be filed any time.

name: Marine Conservation Philippines (MCP)
description: A registered non-profit near Dumaguete that trains international and local volunteers to do scientific scuba surveys of coral reefs, alongside mangrove replanting, plastic clean-ups and school education work. Its volunteers feed data directly into how local governments manage marine protected areas.
volunteer_activities: community and Bantay Dagat training support
how_to_join: Apply through the volunteer application form on their website; new volunteers are taken in every second Monday and picked up free at Dumaguete airport.
requirements: Volunteers must be 18 or older (exceptions for families and school groups), usually stay at least six weeks, have travel insurance and an outbound ticket, and pay a program fee that covers meals, accommodation and dive gear.

name: People and the Sea
description: A non-profit launched in 2015 based on Malapascua Island that supports coastal communities with marine research, waste reduction, sustainable fishing and youth education programmes. It recruits on-site expedition volunteers as well as remote volunteers who can donate specific professional skills.
how_to_join: Apply online through the 'Apply now' form on their website for an on-site expedition placement, or get in touch about volunteering remotely with a particular skill set.
requirements: Expeditions run on published dates with associated costs; applicants apply online and are assessed before placement.

name: Aklan Animal Rescue and Rehabilitation Center (AARRC Philippines)
description: A volunteer-run shelter and rehabilitation centre in Kalibo, Aklan, that rescues stray pets and runs vaccination and neutering work across the province. It also hosts international volunteers and offers simple accommodation for travellers who want to help.
volunteer_activities: cleaning cat kennels and dog enclosures
how_to_join: Fill out the volunteer form on their Volunteering page; the centre says volunteers are welcome at any time of the year.
requirements: The volunteer form asks you to confirm that you are over 16 years old.

name: Bohol Animal Rescue & Kindness (BARK)
description: Described on its own site as the only animal rescue and shelter organisation in Tagbilaran, running a no-kill free-range dog shelter plus the Dogs of Alona trap-neuter-release-manage project in Panglao. It also feeds impounded dogs at the Tagbilaran City Pound and lobbies for better animal welfare laws.
volunteer_activities: daily animal care at the shelter
guest feeding of Dogs of Alona beach animals
how_to_join: The shelter is not open to walk-in visitors, so contact BARK by phone or email to schedule an appointment; their volunteer page invites help with daily animal care and community outreach.
requirements: Appointments must be arranged in advance; no other formal requirements are listed.

name: A Heart for Paws GenSan
description: The first animal-welfare NGO in General Santos City, founded in 2018 to rescue stray, abused and abandoned dogs and cats. It keeps animals in a temporary shelter in Calatao, Tambler and in foster homes, and reports over 150 rescues to date.
volunteer_activities: adoption and responsible pet ownership outreach
how_to_join: Use the 'I want to Volunteer' link on their website or message their Facebook page — the group tells people they can help by volunteering at its shelter.

name: Animal Rescue Rehabilitation & Fostering (ARRF) - Davao, Inc.
description: A non-profit rescue group founded in 2016 by dog and cat advocates that takes in abandoned, neglected and abused animals in Davao City. Because it works largely through community foster homes rather than a big facility, it depends on people who can foster, transport and fundraise.
how_to_join: Use the 'Become a Volunteer' form on the ARRF Davao website, or contact the group by email or through its Facebook page.

name: Bantay Hayop Davao (Shelter for Animal Healing)
description: A Davao City shelter that has taken in and rehabilitated rescued animals for several years and regularly posts open calls for volunteers. It runs scheduled volunteer days so ordinary people can experience a full day of shelter caregiver work.
volunteer_activities: cleaning halls, cages and common grounds
how_to_join: Sign up through the shelter's listing on iVolunteer or message its Facebook page; the group says it sends full details by text after you register.
requirements: Volunteers go to the shelter in Purok 26-B Malagamot, Panacan, Davao City on the scheduled day, and feeding animals is not allowed during volunteer days to avoid dog fights.

name: Bukidnon Animal Welfare Advocates (BAWA)
description: A Bukidnon advocacy group active around Manolo Fortich and Libona that rescues, feeds and cares for animals it describes as voiceless. The group is raising funds to build a permanent shelter and frequently asks its followers to adopt, foster or help transport rescued animals.
volunteer_activities: transporting animals to safety or to adopters
how_to_join: Message the Facebook page or comment on one of its rescue posts saying you want to adopt or help — the group coordinates from there.

name: CDO Animal Welfare Society Inc.
description: A non-government funded, volunteer rescue group in Cagayan de Oro that handles rescues and campaigns for animal rights and awareness. It also partners with the Limketkai Foundation, which operates the Dog Home sanctuary where rescued dogs are rehabilitated and rehomed.
volunteer_activities: shelter support through its Dog Home partnership
how_to_join: Get in touch through the group's Facebook page, where it posts rescue appeals, adoption calls and requests for volunteers.

name: Davao Animal Rescue Volunteers (Sonia's Home of Animal Rescue)
description: An SEC-registered non-profit rescue group in Davao City that also runs Sonia's Home of Animal Rescue, a shelter in Toril for stray, abandoned and abused animals. The group rallies the public around feeding runs and donation drives rather than relying on paid staff.
how_to_join: Message the Facebook page to volunteer; the group regularly posts invitations for the public to join, support and donate to its stray-feeding activities.

name: Dogs Camp Iligan
description: An Iligan City shelter that gives stray and impounded dogs a second chance and currently houses more than 20 dogs. It runs on donations and volunteer help, and has links with earlier Iligan rescue efforts such as PART-Iligan and Iligan Stray Feeders.
volunteer_activities: helping with adoption and fundraising appeals
how_to_join: Message the Dogs Camp Iligan Facebook page to ask about volunteering, fostering or donating.

name: Hearts for Paws Butuan City
description: A local non-government animal welfare group founded in October 2017 that rescues and cares for stray and abandoned dogs and cats in Butuan City. It runs a shelter, works with the city dog pound and publishes adoption and rescue updates.
volunteer_activities: shelter cleaning, feeding and animal care
how_to_join: Message the Facebook page to volunteer; the group has posted open calls for helping hands at its shelter.

name: Limketkai Foundation Cat Home
description: A cat rescue sanctuary in Malaybalay, Bukidnon run by the Limketkai Foundation, providing shelter, veterinary care and adoption preparation for abandoned and stray cats. Volunteers are described as the backbone of its daily operations.
volunteer_activities: socializing cats to prepare them for adoption
how_to_join: Sign up through the Volunteer section of the Limketkai Foundation website and ask to be placed on animal care at the Cat Home.
requirements: The foundation states that no special skills are required for volunteering.

name: Limketkai Foundation Dog Home
description: A rescue and rehabilitation sanctuary for abandoned, neglected and injured dogs in Cagayan de Oro, operated by the Limketkai Foundation together with CDO Animal Welfare Society. Dogs receive vaccination, spay/neuter and behavioural assessment before being matched with adopters, and a daily volunteer dog-walking routine is part of the program.
how_to_join: Go to the foundation's Get Involved page and use the Volunteer 'Get in touch' option, asking to be assigned to animal care at the Dog Home.
requirements: The foundation says no special skills are required — just a willingness to show up.

name: Paw Savers Zamboanga
description: A Zamboanga City group that shelters rescued dogs and cats taken off the streets or handed over to it, and has been building a new shelter site with additional kennels. It runs entirely on volunteers and public donations.
volunteer_activities: caring for rescued dogs and cats at the shelter
helping with shelter construction and maintenance
how_to_join: Send a message to the Facebook page — the group posts calls for volunteers alongside its donation appeals.

name: Purpaws (People United to Rescue Pets that are Abused, Wasted and Sick)
description: A non-profit volunteer network that started in General Santos City and has since opened chapters in Cotabato City and in the MAKIMA towns of South Cotabato. It rescues abused, abandoned and sick pets and pushes for responsible pet ownership in the communities it serves.
volunteer_activities: adoption and outreach drives with local chapters
how_to_join: Message the Purpaws Facebook page or join one of its chapter groups to be brought into rescue and campaign activities.

name: Philippine Eagle Foundation
description: A Davao-based conservation non-profit that runs the Philippine Eagle Center in Malagos, where injured and orphaned eagles are cared for with the aim of returning them to the wild. Volunteers help with its education, research and events programs, and the center also offers a shorter voluntourist option for visitors who can only give a day.
volunteer_activities: helping with research and nest-monitoring work
working at the Philippine Eagle Center
carbon forest planting through the Voluntourist program
how_to_join: Fill out the Volunteer Application Form linked from the foundation's volunteer page. If you only have a weekend, you can instead schedule a Voluntour activity, which the center runs with a limited number of participants.
requirements: An application form must be submitted in advance; the center says it accepts 15 volunteers per weekday and 15 voluntourists on weekends.

name: Be Pawsitive Spay and Neuter
description: Be Pawsitive is an SEC-registered animal welfare group in General Luna, Siargao, focused on controlling the island's pet population through spaying and neutering and on promoting responsible pet ownership. Its main vehicle is the AquaFlask Be Pawsitive Run, an annual 5K/10K fundraising event whose proceeds support spay-and-neuter programs. The organisation looks for volunteers to help stage the run and to spread the message around the island.
volunteer_activities: helping stage the annual Be Pawsitive fun run
registration desk and on-site participant support
sharing responsible pet ownership and spay/neuter advocacy
how_to_join: Register through the Volunteer page on the Be Pawsitive website, or use the Contact Us page to reach the team by email or Instagram (@bepawsitive.siargao) about other ways to help.

name: Youth for Animals - UP Mindanao
description: A student-run chapter of the Philippine Animal Welfare Society's Youth for Animals network at UP Mindanao in Davao City. Youth for Animals is PAWS' university-based youth cluster, so the chapter exists to carry animal welfare advocacy into campus and community settings.
volunteer_activities: campaigns and events together with PAWS
helping look after community animals on campus
how_to_join: Follow the chapter's Facebook page and message it directly to ask about recruitment and upcoming activities.
